items.title: No comparison of tracking approaches in one place
items.whyItMatters: Each approach is reported in a different setting and design, so champions quote the figure that suits them.
items.opportunity: Tabulate every approach with its design, setting, finding types and completion definition.

items.title: Completion figures are not comparable
items.whyItMatters: Windows, denominators and finding types differ between studies, so a single number per approach would mislead.
items.opportunity: Record window and denominator with every figure and refuse to pool.

items.title: Patients without a primary care clinician and emergency-only patients
items.whyItMatters: They complete follow-up far less often (claim c3) and are where alerts fail (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Extract results for these groups from every report and state which approaches were never tested with them.

items.title: Language and interpreter needs are rarely reported
items.whyItMatters: Few failure reports describe patients who do not speak the local language (claim c4), and letters were English-only in the retrieved study.
items.opportunity: Search specifically for language-related follow-up and report the gap if nothing is found.

items.title: An unverified benchmark is circulating
items.whyItMatters: A model lead presents a national benchmark as a landmark with a DOI that no retrieval returned; citing it would anchor the committee on an unchecked number.
items.opportunity: Check its identifier before any use; until then it is not evidence.

errorsFound: The first scan reply labelled an unretrieved national benchmark as a landmark with a DOI; the label is not verification, and the lead stays unverified.
reevaluation: The gaps favour a narrative review organised by failure point, with completion definitions kept visible, equity results extracted throughout, and unverified figures kept out of the committee report.
summary: Five gaps; the missing comparison, incomparable figures and the groups most often missed are high severity.
